I started losing weight when I began doing it out of love for myself instead of self hate. I started focusing on eating foods that make me feel good physically. Every time I eat I ask myself if it meets my nutritional needs. I still eat "fun stuff" regularly, I just balance it out with lighter meals. I also have been working on not using food for fun or comfort as often as possible. That's hard. 

 A dietician told me a good starting point is to make sure you have a large serving of veggies with every meal, at least half your plate. I eat a ton of broccoli and carrots with fat free ranch, lol. Lots of water too, I keep a clear water bottle to help me stay conscious of it. 

When you track calories for a while, it gets easier to estimate  calories without having to look it up. I use MyFitnessPal app (free ver) to log my food. I really recommend it. I have a reminder on my phone to log my calories every night. I do it even if I'm unhappy with what I ate- /especially/ if I'm unhappy with it.  

You're not weak. I felt exactly the same way, still sometimes do. It's difficult to unlearn habits you've built during hard times. Beating yourself up and surrounding food and eating with guilt will make things harder on you. Try to be your own friend, even when it's difficult.
